instruction: Browse Star Wars toys for kids and sort by lowest price.

metadata.explanation: Task requires browsing Star Wars products in Kids/Toys category and sorting by price low-high (S=4). Maintains same pattern and complexity as original task. Reuses existing evaluator infrastructure.

llm_judge_reasons: The evaluator uses very specific HTML class selectors (pmpSearch_breadcrumb, sbSelector) that may not exist on the actual Kohl's website
The class_multiObject_li approach assumes a specific HTML structure (<li class='catAllProducts'><span>) that may not match the actual page structure
The evaluator does not have fallback mechanisms if the expected HTML classes are not found
While the logic is sound in theory, there's high risk of runtime failure due to selector mismatches with the actual Kohl's website HTML
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Verify that the class names 'pmpSearch_breadcrumb' and 'sbSelector' actually exist on Kohl's website for this search scenario
Add more flexible selectors or multiple fallback selectors for breadcrumbs and sort dropdown elements
Consider using class_multiObject_flexible instead of class_multiObject_li to handle varying HTML structures
Test the actual HTML structure of Kohl's search results page to ensure selectors will match at runtime
Add explicit validation in the getter to log when expected elements are not found, improving debuggability
